commits_analyzed.message: validation iter-24: Thompson posteriors live (RETURN fix); execution metrics verified; create-shape-provider-goal post-fix status; critical blockers (task-generation-flooding, topology-queue)
commits_analyzed.what_return_fix_means: SurrealDB 3.x RETURN shorthand syntax 'RETURN { id, total_executions }' was causing a parse error in execution-traces.ts. The applyOutcomeToPosteriors callback never fired on trace writes. Fix: changed to explicit RETURN syntax (per c48c4333 submodule update). Result: Thompson posteriors now increment on every trace outcome.
commits_analyzed.what_task_generation_flooding_means: TASK_GENERATION_ENABLED env var is not set to false in /etc/substrate/env. A TaskGenerator process fires every 5 minutes, adding 10 debug__* / optimize_* tasks to the boredom:queue:critical Redis sorted set. ZCARD reached 1232 — topology tasks are enqueued but never reached because debug/optimize tasks are ahead of them in the priority queue. The queue fills faster than it can drain.
commits_analyzed.what_topology_queue_means: The topology_harness_next Redis key exists but the topology templates are NOT in the boredom:queue:critical sorted set (the active execution queue). Even if seeded, they are not being dispatched to goal-host. Two sub-issues: (1) task-generation-flooding blocking queue drain, (2) topology goals need explicit ZADD to boredom:queue:critical or a POST /v2/activities/boredom/enqueue call.

commits_analyzed.message: fix(substrate): assign unique vesselId/endpoint to development-vessel and concept-db
commits_analyzed.what_vesselid_fix_does: Prior to this fix, both development-vessel and concept-db were reading VESSEL_ID=substrate-local and VESSEL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8080 from the global /etc/substrate/env file. They were registering with the same vesselId in the discovery registry, overwriting each other. concept-db won the last heartbeat, leaving development-vessel's 30 shapes invisible. Fix: added per-vessel Environment= overrides in each .service unit (development-vessel gets VESSEL_ID=development-vessel-local, VESSEL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8090; concept-db gets VESSEL_ID=concept-db-local, VESSEL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8260). Removed the global VESSEL_ID/VESSEL_ENDPOINT lines from gen-env.sh. After fix: 5 distinct vessels in discovery (54 shapes total vs prior 4/24). F-050 resolved.
files_changed: scripts/substrate/gen-env.sh (-4 lines: removed global VESSEL_ID + VESSEL_ENDPOINT)

create_shape_provider_goal_root_cause.regression_explanation: The '24%→0% regression' the validator observed is explained by the composition chain. Prior to the RETURN fix + vesselId fix, create-shape-provider-goal was dispatched as a top-level goal. Now it is dispatched as a CHILD within coverage-tick's composition chain: coverage-tick → validator-dispatch → slot-binding → create-shape-provider-goal. The child execution has impulse_count=0 (no impulses passed down the chain), causing instant failure (1ms) before any task executes.
create_shape_provider_goal_root_cause.all_task_count_zero: ALL executions in the chain have task_count=0. Tasks are executing (evidenced by duration: coverage-tick=44s, validator-dispatch=43s, slot-binding=36s) but not being written to the trace. This is a separate finding: task storage gap in IAS executor for composed executions.
create_shape_provider_goal_root_cause.failure_reason: create-shape-provider-goal receives no impulses (impulse_count=0) when dispatched as a composition child. The activity requires input shapes (activity_metrics, activity_template, goal, execution_trace, etc.) that are not propagated through the composition chain. The activity fails before executing any task because required inputs are absent.
create_shape_provider_goal_root_cause.f036_update: OPEN with new root cause: composition dispatch provides no impulses. This is distinct from the resolver registration issue (resolved in iter-022). The activity_recommendation resolver is registered but the activity fails before calling it because slot-binding did not pass impulses forward.

task_generation_flooding_explanation.what_it_is: A TaskGenerator process in the substrate runs every 5 minutes, adding debug__* and optimize_* task variants to the boredom:queue:critical Redis sorted set. With TASK_GENERATION_ENABLED not set to false, the queue fills with debugging and optimization tasks faster than the boredom-vessel can drain them. ZCARD reached 1232 at iter-24 observation.
task_generation_flooding_explanation.consequence: Topology goals (coverage-tick, substrate-health-tick, probe-*) are pushed to the back of the queue by the continuously-generated debug/optimize tasks. They never reach execution.
task_generation_flooding_explanation.fix: Set TASK_GENERATION_ENABLED=false in /etc/substrate/env and reload services. OR: Implement a priority scheme where topology tasks preempt debug/optimize tasks.
task_generation_flooding_explanation.status: Still open per iter-24 observation. This investigation could not verify queue ZCARD directly without redis-cli access.

topology_queue_explanation.what_it_is: The topology_harness_next Redis key exists (tracking which topology goal is next) but topology goals are not in the boredom:queue:critical sorted set where boredom-vessel reads from. Two causes: (1) task-generation-flooding fills the queue with other tasks, (2) topology templates may need explicit enqueuing via POST /v2/activities/boredom/enqueue.
topology_queue_explanation.status: Likely partially resolved by vesselId fix: now that development-vessel is properly registered, boredom can discover coverage-tick and dispatch it directly without going through the Redis queue (evidenced by the successful coverage-tick trace at 09:40:19Z).

new_findings.title: task_count=0 for all executions in composition chains — tasks not stored in execution trace

evidence.command: curl -sf -H 'Authorization: ApiKey $APIKEY' 'http://localhost:18080/v2/activities/execution-traces?limit=200' | python3 -c 'show task_count for executions'
evidence.excerpt: coverage-tick: task_count=0, dur=44122ms; validator-dispatch: task_count=0, dur=43664ms; slot-binding: task_count=0, dur=36376ms; create-shape-provider-goal: task_count=0, dur=1ms

new_findings.note: Every execution in the 200-trace window has task_count=0. Durations (44s, 43s, 36s) prove tasks ARE executing. The IAS executor is not writing per-task records to activity_execution_traces. Affects: (a) per-task impulse grouping for co-occurrence learning, (b) root cause diagnosis of create-shape-provider-goal failures, (c) resolver performance tracking.
new_findings.operator_remediation: Investigate IAS executor task write path. Per-task records should be appended to the trace during execution. Likely the ias-executor-ts GoalHost task completion handler is not calling the task write endpoint.

new_findings.title: Thompson alpha systematically under-counted by ~4x for high-volume templates

evidence.excerpt: validator-dispatch: n=456, ok=456, alpha=100 (expected 457, ratio=0.22); slot-binding: n=63, ok=63, alpha=16 (expected 64, ratio=0.25); create-shape-provider-goal: n=66, fail=66, beta=17 (expected 67, ratio=0.25). Low-n templates: ratio close to 1.0.

new_findings.note: Direction is correct; under-counting does not affect selection ordering. validator-dispatch EV=0.99 >> create-shape-provider-goal EV=0.056. Likely cause: batching or sampling writes at rate ~1/4 for high-volume templates. Not lift-blocking but represents sampling loss in the learning loop.
new_findings.operator_remediation: Investigate applyOutcomeToPosteriors write path for batching configuration. If intentional sampling, document the sample rate. If unintentional, identify where the 3/4 of writes are dropped.
